trans-saharan-trade.name: Trans-Saharan trade
trans-saharan-trade.summary: Trade across the Sahara linking North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa, peaking from the 8th to the early 17th centuries and carried by camel caravans sometimes thousands strong, guided by Berbers.

gao.name: Gao
gao.summary: A city in Mali on the River Niger, once a major trans-Saharan trade hub; it became capital of the Songhai Empire under Sunni Ali (1464–1492) after earlier being part of the Mali Empire.

ghana-empire.name: Ghana Empire
ghana-empire.summary: An ancient West African empire based in what is now southeast Mauritania and western Mali, first mentioned in writing in 830 CE; it became a vassal of the Mali Empire in the 13th century.

takrur.name: Takrur
takrur.summary: A state based along the Senegal River in what is now Senegal, at its height in the 11th and 12th centuries alongside the Ghana Empire.

bura-culture.name: Bura culture
bura-culture.summary: Iron Age archaeological culture, dated from around the 3rd to 13th century CE, centered in the lower Niger River valley of Niger and Burkina Faso, known for distinctive clay, iron and stone artifacts including early terracotta equestrian statuettes.

igbo-ukwu.name: Igbo-Ukwu
igbo-ukwu.summary: A town in southeastern Nigeria whose nearby archaeological complex yielded elaborate copper, bead and ivory objects from roughly the 9th to 12th centuries, showing sophisticated early craft and trade.

nok-culture.name: Nok culture
nok-culture.summary: An ancient population in what is now Nigeria, named for the village where its terracotta sculptures were first found in 1928, existing from roughly 1500 BCE to 1 CE.

gao-saney.name: Gao-Saney
gao-saney.summary: An archaeological site near Gao in Mali, likely the historical trading town of Sarneh, occupied roughly 700–1100 CE and involved in glass and copper trade networks.

djenn-djenno.name: Djenné-Djeno
djenn-djenno.summary: Ancient urban site in Mali's Niger River Valley, occupied from about 250 BC to 1400 AD, among the oldest known cities in West Africa and evidence of early long-distance trade.

charles-thurstan-shaw.name: Thurstan Shaw
charles-thurstan-shaw.summary: English archaeologist (1914–2013), the first trained specialist to work in British West Africa, whose excavations at Igbo-Ukwu revealed a sophisticated 9th-century bronze-working culture.

list-of-rulers-of-nri.name: Eze Nri
list-of-rulers-of-nri.summary: Title of the ruler of the Kingdom of Nri, holding both religious and political authority, with the role still held today.

aoudaghost.name: Aoudaghost
aoudaghost.summary: A former Berber trading town in what is now Mauritania, an oasis at the southern end of a trans-Saharan caravan route.

kanem-bornu-empire.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
kanem-bornu-empire.summary: A long-lived empire around Lake Chad, founded around 700 CE and sustained by trans-Saharan trade, later re-centered from Kanem to the Bornu region after the 14th century.

soninke-people.name: Soninke
soninke-people.summary: A West African Mande-speaking ethnic group who founded the ancient empire of Ghana (Wagadou), around 200 to 1240 CE, later spreading widely as traders.

lamtuna.name: Lamtuna
lamtuna.summary: Nomadic Berber tribe of the Sanhaja confederation, once living from Sous to the Adrar Plateau. Many moved north during the Almoravid period, and they are now based in southern Mauritania.

sanhaja.name: Sanhaja
sanhaja.summary: Large Berber tribal confederation, alongside the Zanata and Masmuda. Many tribes across Algeria, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Senegal, Tunisia and Western Sahara carry the name.

al-khwarizmi.name: Al-Khwarizmi
al-khwarizmi.summary: A mathematician, astronomer and geographer (c. 780-850) of the Islamic Golden Age who worked at Baghdad's House of Wisdom and is regarded as the father of algebra.

al-bakri.name: Al-Bakri
al-bakri.summary: Arab Andalusian historian and geographer (c. 1040-1094) whose writings on the medieval Maghreb are an early source on West African kingdoms.

mu-ammad-ibn-ibr-h-m-al-faz-r.name: Al-Fazari
mu-ammad-ibn-ibr-h-m-al-faz-r.summary: Arab philosopher, mathematician and astronomer who died in 796 or 806.

idrisid-dynasty.name: Idrisid dynasty
idrisid-dynasty.summary: An Arab Muslim dynasty that ruled most of present-day Morocco and parts of western Algeria from 788 to 974, founded by Idris I and central to the early Islamization of Morocco.

al-ya-qubi.name: Al-Ya'qubi
al-ya-qubi.summary: An Arab Muslim historian and geographer who died in 897/8.

al-masudi.name: Al-Masudi
al-masudi.summary: A historian, geographer and traveler (c. 896–956), sometimes called the 'Herodotus of the Arabs,' best known for his magnum opus The Meadows of Gold, blending history, geography and biography.

abakaliki.name: Abakaliki
abakaliki.summary: The capital city of Ebonyi State in southeastern Nigeria, home mainly to Igbo people and once headquarters of the Ogoja province.

kingdom-of-benin.name: Kingdom of Benin
kingdom-of-benin.summary: A long-lived kingdom in what is now southern Nigeria, centered on Benin City, renowned by the 15th–16th centuries for trade with Europe and for its bronze, ivory and brass artistry, before British annexation in 1897.

koro-toro.name: Koro Toro
koro-toro.summary: Settlement in the southern Borkou Region of Chad where the fossil hominin Australopithecus bahrelghazali was found in 1995. It also hosts a notorious desert prison.

kingdom-of-nri.name: Kingdom of Nri
kingdom-of-nri.summary: A precolonial Igbo ritual polity in southeastern Nigeria whose sacred ruler, the Eze Nri, held authority through religion and title-taking rather than military force, dating from around the 10th century.

igboland.name: Igboland
igboland.summary: The cultural and linguistic homeland of the Igbo people in southern Nigeria, an informal region with no official government, spanning several states and diverse local traditions.

michael-a-gomez.name: Michael Gomez
michael-a-gomez.summary: An American historian and Silver Professor at New York University, born in 1955, known for his scholarship on West Africa, the African diaspora, Islam and slavery.

african-dominion.name: African Dominion
african-dominion.summary: A history book by Michael A. Gomez tracing empire-building in early and medieval West Africa's Middle Niger Valley, from the mid-6th century to Songhay's fall to Moroccan rule in 1591.

songhai-empire.name: Songhai Empire
songhai-empire.summary: A major West African state that flourished in the 15th and 16th centuries, eventually surpassing the Mali Empire in area, wealth and power under Sonni Ali and later the Askia dynasty.

girgam.name: Girgam
girgam.summary: The royal chronicle of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, written in Arabic, listing 69 rulers and details of their reigns; discovered by traveller Heinrich Barth in 1851.

heinrich-barth.name: Heinrich Barth
heinrich-barth.summary: German explorer of Africa (1821–1865), regarded as one of the greatest European explorers of the continent for his careful documentation of cultures and oral histories.

ahmad-ibn-tulun.name: Ahmad ibn Tulun
ahmad-ibn-tulun.summary: Founder of the Tulunid dynasty that ruled Egypt and Syria from 868 to 905, who built an independent administration and military and constructed a new capital, al-Qata'i.

ibn-hawqal.name: Ibn Hawqal
ibn-hawqal.summary: A 10th-century Arab geographer and chronicler who traveled widely from 943 to 969 and wrote 'The Face of the Earth,' completed in 977.

sijilmasa.name: Sijilmasa
sijilmasa.summary: A medieval Moroccan trading city at the northern edge of the Sahara, an important terminus of trans-Saharan trade routes until the 14th century.

eri-king.name: Eri
eri-king.summary: Legendary founding ancestor of the Igbo Umu-eri groups, said to have settled the Anambra river valley and fathered the lines that founded Aguleri, the Kingdom of Nri and other communities.

fiku-nim.name: Ìfikuánim
fiku-nim.summary: The first king of the Nri Kingdom according to Igbo oral tradition; his reign is traditionally dated to 1043, though one historian places it around 1225.

djembe.name: Djembe
djembe.summary: Rope-tuned, skin-covered goblet drum originally from Senegal, played bare-handed and widely used across West Africa, prized for its expressive range of sounds.

griot.name: Griot
griot.summary: A West African oral historian, storyteller and musician who preserves cultural traditions and often serves as an advisor or mediator, sometimes within families passed down generations.
